newsitem.title: MADAGASCAR: Former Madagascan president seeks backing in poll.
newsitem.headline: Former Madagascan president seeks backing in poll.

text.p: Former Madagascan president Albert Zafy, seeking re-election in a run-off presidential poll on December 29, said on Tuesday if he won he would reappoint his former prime minister.
Zafy paid tribute to his former prime minister Norbert Ratsirahonana for clearing the way in November for a resumption of aid to Madagascar from the International Monetary Fund.
Zafy made his announcement after talks with Ratsirahonana.

Ratsirahonana, who came fourth in the first round of presidential elections on November 3 with 10.14 percent of the vote, said on Sunday he had a neutral role in the second round and would not come out for either of the two candidates.
Political analysts said Tuesday's promise by Zafy was aimed at weakening support for his opponent in the second round former military leader Didier Ratsiraka, who looked well placed to win.
Millionaire businessman Herizo Razafimahaleo, who took 15.13 percent of the vote in the first round, has thrown the weight of his Leader Fanilo party behind Ratsiraka for the second round.
In the first round, Ratsiraka, a 60-year-old retired admiral, won 36.61 percent against 23.39 for Zafy.
The presidential election was called after Zafy, 69, who was elected president in place of Ratsiraka in 1993, was impeached by parliament in July for abuse of his authority.

The strength of support for Ratsiraka surprised many. He was reviled by many of his people in the early 1990s for using the army to resist the pro-democracy movement on the island, which has a population of 14 million, most of whom live in chronic poverty.
